newsitem.title: GERMANY: German DAX index seeks to stay above 3,800 points.
newsitem.headline: German DAX index seeks to stay above 3,800 points.

text.p: German shares lost steam in bourse dealings on Monday, ending the session lower as the DAX index failed to close above the key level of 3,800 points.
The DAX index closed down 9.64 points at 3,785.77 points, while the IBIS DAX was down 15.91 points at 3,794.01 points in post-bourse computer dealings.
Dealings in the afternoon were expected to be relatively steady and focus on Wall Street movements.
But little action was expected in New York ahead of Tuesday's U.S. Federal Reserve policy meeting, at which no change in interest rates was expected.

The small losses on Monday did little to change market sentiment and the cautiously optimistic view for the DAX to climb above 4,000 points in second half of 1997 after the DAX ended the first half up 31 percent from the start of the year.

Low interest rates and stable inflation, along with favourable profit developments from many major German companies and strong demand for shares, will continue to underpin the market in the second half of the year, some dealers said.
Among specific shares on Monday, chemical and automotive stocks were the focus of trading during the day.
Luxury carmaker Porsche AG was a top percentage gainer, rising 190 marks to 2,320 marks due to the stronger dollar, while Volkswagen AG gained 32 marks to 1,337 marks.

Chemical group Bayer AG ended up two pfennigs at 67.02 marks, while Hoechst AG gained 1.38 marks to 73.98 marks after the group said it would take a breather on acquisitions in its pharmaceuticals division.
